parts.label: (i)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: State or imply a correct normal vector to either plane, e.g. $2\mathbf i+3\mathbf j-\mathbf k$ or $\mathbf i-2\mathbf j+\mathbf k$ [B1]. Carry out the correct scalar-product process for the normals [M1]. Using the correct modulus process, divide the scalar product by the product of the moduli and evaluate the inverse cosine [M1]. Obtain $56.9^\circ$ or $0.994$ radians [A1]. Total 4.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.answer: $\mathbf r=4\mathbf j+11\mathbf k+\lambda(\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-7\mathbf k)$, or equivalent.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: EITHER carry out a complete strategy for finding a point on the line $l$ [M1] and obtain such a point, e.g. $(1,1,4)$ [A1]. Then EITHER state a correct equation for a direction vector $a\mathbf i+b\mathbf j+c\mathbf k$, e.g. $2a+3b-c=0$ [B1]; state a second equation, e.g. $a-2b+c=0$, and solve for one ratio such as $a:b$ [M1]; obtain $a:b:c=1:-3:-7$, or equivalent [A1]; and state $\mathbf r=\mathbf i+\mathbf j+4\mathbf k+\lambda(\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-7\mathbf k)$ [A1]. OR1 attempt the vector product of the two normals [M1], obtain two correct components [A1], obtain $\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-7\mathbf k$, or equivalent [A1], and state the correct vector equation [A1]. OR2 obtain a second point, e.g. $(0,4,11)$ [B1], subtract position vectors [M1], obtain $\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-7\mathbf k$, or equivalent [A1], and state $\mathbf r=4\mathbf j+11\mathbf k+\mu(\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-7\mathbf k)$, or equivalent [A1]. OR3 express one variable in terms of a second [M1], obtain e.g. $y=4-3x$ [A1], express the third variable in terms of the second [M1], obtain e.g. $z=11-7x$ [A1], form a vector equation [M1], and state $\mathbf r=4\mathbf j+11\mathbf k+\lambda(\mathbf i-3\mathbf j-7\mathbf k)$ [A1]. OR4 express one variable in terms of a second [M1], obtain e.g. $x=4/3-y/3$ [A1], express that variable in terms of the third [M1], obtain e.g. $x=11/7-z/7$ [A1], form a vector equation [M1], and obtain the correct equivalent equation [A1]. Total 6.
